policies.description: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields. For the update_sla_definition tool the mandatory field is sla_def_id, which must be provided and correspond to an existing SLA definition before the update is performed.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Operations must be performed one validated action at a time. The update_sla_definition call must be the sole operation in the request and should only proceed if all required data is present and the current SLA record state allows the update.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: Metrics tracked for SLA records are limited to target_mins. When updating an SLA definition, only the target_mins field (and other allowed fields) may be modified; attempts to add or change unsupported metric fields should be rejected.

When an incident is on hold for specific reasons, the SLA timer must be paused. Updates to an SLA definition must not conflict with this rule; for example, the pause_on_pending flag may be toggled but the system must still enforce pausing under the defined conditions.
references: SLA Pause: The SLA timer must be paused (stage = paused) when the Incident is in stage = on_hold and the on_hold_reason is one of the following enumerations: Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.

policies.description: If an SLA exceeds its duration, the incident’s escalation flag must be set to true and a notification sent to the Manager. Updating an SLA definition must preserve this behavior; the active or target_mins changes must not disable required breach handling.
references: Breach: If the SLA exceeds its duration (stage = breached), the escalation flag on the Incident must be set to true, and an automatic notification sent to the Manager.

policies.policy_name: Role‑Based Access for SLA Definition Updates
policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role are authorized to call the update_sla_definition tool. The Administrator role has Full CRUD access across all tables, whereas other roles (Manager, Agent, Reporter) do not have update privileges on SLA definition records. If a non‑Administrator attempts an update, the operation must be halted with a 403 Forbidden response.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: If the caller’s role lacks the authority to perform an update_sla_definition operation, the system must respond with a 403 Forbidden error and must not proceed with any changes.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: When the update_sla_definition endpoint returns a rate‑limit error, the assistant must pause the request and retry using an exponential backoff strategy instead of immediately retrying or proceeding.
references: Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.description: Before invoking the update_sla_definition tool, the assistant must verify that the provided `sla_def_id` corresponds to an existing SLA definition record in the system. The operation must not proceed if the identifier cannot be resolved, and the assistant should return an appropriate error indicating that the SLA definition was not found.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.policy_name: Record Conflict Handling (409 Conflict) for SLA Updates
policies.description: If the SLA definition record is locked, being modified by another process, or otherwise in a state that prevents the update, the assistant must halt the operation and return a `409 Conflict` error. No changes may be applied when such a conflict is detected.
references: 409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.
